  "content": "package com.keeplearning.auth.keycloak.controller\n\nimport com.keeplearning.auth.keycloak.service.AccountUserRoleService\nimport org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*\n\n/**\n * Simplified user role management endpoints for ECS integration.\n * These endpoints use email instead of userId for easier integration.\n */\n@RestController\n@RequestMapping(\"/api/account/users\")\nclass AccountUserRoleController(\n    private val service: AccountUserRoleService\n) {\n\n    @GetMapping(\"/{email}/roles\")\n    suspend fun getUserRoles(\n        @PathVariable email: String\n    ): Map<String, Any> {\n        return service.getUserRolesByEmail(email)\n    }\n\n    @PutMapping(\"/{email}/roles\")\n    suspend fun updateUserRoles(\n        @PathVariable email: String,\n        @RequestBody request: Map<String, List<String>>\n    ): Map<String, Any> {\n        val roles = request[\"roles\"] ?: emptyList()\n        val approvalScopes = request[\"approval_scopes\"] ?: emptyList()\n        return service.updateUserRolesByEmail(email, roles, approvalScopes)\n    }\n}\n"
}

 suspend fun getUserRolesByEmail(email: String): Map<String, Any> {\n        logger.debug(\"Getting roles for user with email: $email\")\n\n        // Find user in Keycloak by email\n        val user = keycloakAdminClient.getUserByEmail(DEFAULT_REALM, email)\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, \"User not found with email: $email\")\n\n        val userId = user.id\n keycloakAdminClient.getClientByClientId(DEFAULT_REALM, ECS_CLIENT_ID)\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, \"ECS client not found\")\n\n        val clientUuid = ecsClient.id\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"Client UUID not available\")\n\n        // Get user's client roles\n        val clientRoles = keycloakAdminClient.getUserClientRoleMappings(DEFAULT_REALM, userId, clientUuid)\n        val roleNames = clientRoles.map { it.name }\n\n        // Get user's approval_scopes attribute\n        val approvalScopes = user.attributes?.get(\"approval_scopes\") ?: emptyList()\n\n        return mapOf(\n            \"roles\" to roleNames,\n            \"approval_scopes\" to approvalScopes\n        )\n    }\n\n    suspend fun updateUserRolesByEmail(\n        email: String,\n        roles: List<String>,\n        approvalScopes: List<String>\n    ): Map<String, Any> {\n        logger.info(\"Updating roles for user: $email - roles: $roles, approvalScopes: $approvalScopes\")\n\n        // Find user in Keycloak by email\n        val user = keycloakAdminClient.getUserByEmail(DEFAULT_REALM, email)\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, \"User not found with email: $email\")\n\n        val userId = user.id\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"User ID not available\")\n\n        // Get ECS client UUID\n        val ecsClient = keycloakAdminClient.getClientByClientId(DEFAULT_REALM, ECS_CLIENT_ID)\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, \"ECS client not found\")\n\n        val clientUuid = ecsClient.id\n            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"Client UUID not available\")\n\n        // Get all available client roles\n        val allClientRoles = keycloakAdminClient.getClientRoles(DEFAULT_REALM, clientUuid)\n\n        // Get current role assignments\n        val currentRoles = keycloakAdminClient.getUserClientRoleMappings(DEFAULT_REALM, userId, clientUuid)\n        val currentRoleNames = currentRoles.map { it.name }.toSet()\n\n        // Determine roles to add and remove\n        val rolesToAdd = roles.filter { it !in currentRoleNames }\n        val rolesToRemove = currentRoleNames.filter { it !in roles }\n\n        // Remove roles no longer assigned\n        if (rolesToRemove.isNotEmpty()) {\n            val roleReps = rolesToRemove.mapNotNull { roleName ->\n                allClientRoles.find { it.name == roleName }\n            }\n            if (roleReps.isNotEmpty()) {\n                keycloakAdminClient.removeUserClientRoleMappings(DEFAULT_REALM, userId, clientUuid, roleReps)\n                logger.info(\"Removed roles $rolesToRemove from user $email\")\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add new roles\n        if (rolesToAdd.isNotEmpty()) {\n            val roleReps = rolesToAdd.mapNotNull { roleName ->\n                allClientRoles.find { it.name == roleName }\n                    ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, \"Role '$roleName' not found for ECS client\")\n            }\n            keycloakAdminClient.addUserClientRoleMappings(DEFAULT_REALM, userId, clientUuid, roleReps)\n            logger.info(\"Added roles $rolesToAdd to user $email\")\n        }\n\n        // Update approval_scopes attribute\n        val updatedAttributes = (user.attributes ?: emptyMap()).toMutableMap()\n        if (approvalScopes.isNotEmpty()) {\n            updatedAttributes[\"approval_scopes\"] = approvalScopes\n        } else {\n            updatedAttributes.remove(\"approval_scopes\")\n        }\n\n        val updatedUser = user.copy(attributes = updatedAttributes)\n        keycloakAdminClient.updateUser(DEFAULT_REALM, userId, updatedUser)\n        logger.info(\"Updated approval_scopes for user $email: $approvalScopes\")\n\n        return mapOf(\n            \"roles\" to roles,\n            \"approval_scopes\" to approvalScopes\n        )\n    }\n}\n"
}

## 🎉 WorkPlan Approval Scopes Feature - Complete!

Great news! The **WorkPlan Approval Scopes** feature was already **95% implemented** across all services. I've completed the final 5% by adding the missing auth backend integration.

### ✅ What Was Already Implemented

#### **1. Keycloak Setup** (ecs-integration-tests)
- ✅ `approver` client role on `ecs` client
- ✅ `approval-scopes` client scope with protocol mapper
- ✅ Maps `approval_scopes` user attribute to JWT claim (multivalued)

#### **2. ECS Backend** (ecs-jarvis-core)
- ✅ `ApprovalScope` helper - extracts scopes from JWT
- ✅ Scope enforcement in `approveActivityType()` and `rejectActivityType()`
- ✅ `getPendingApprovalsForApprover()` - queries by scopes
- ✅ Controller endpoints with JWT scope extraction
- ✅ Faculty role management proxy controller
- ✅ Repository queries for pending approvals by type

#### **3. ECS Frontend** (kos-ecs)
- ✅ Role store with `approverScopes`, `isApprover`, `canApproveType()`
- ✅ WorkPlan Approvals page with filtering, review dialog, approve/reject
- ✅ User Roles & Permissions page with real API integration
- ✅ Navigation items conditionally shown for approvers
- ✅ Route guards for `/workplan-approvals`

#### **4. Integration Test** (ecs-integration-tests)
- ✅ Comprehensive end-to-end test covering all scenarios
- ✅ Creates approver user, verifies JWT claims, tests scope enforcement
- ✅ Validates 403 for out-of-scope actions, 200 for in-scope

### 🆕 What I Added

#### **Auth Backend Email-Based Endpoints**
Created wrapper endpoints for ECS integration:

**New files:**
- `AccountUserRoleController.kt` - Email-based user role management
  - `GET /api/account/users/{email}/roles` - Get user's roles and approval_scopes
  - `PUT /api/account/users/{email}/roles` - Update roles and approval_scopes

- `AccountUserRoleService.kt` - Service implementation
  - Looks up user by email in Keycloak
  - Manages `ecs` client roles (administrator, approver, faculty)
  - Manages `approval_scopes` attribute (research, teaching, institutional-service)

These endpoints bridge the gap between the ECS backend (which works with emails) and the existing Keycloak user management service (which works with user IDs).

### 🔄 How It Works

```
1. Admin assigns roles via ECS Frontend (User Roles & Permissions page)
   ↓
2. ECS Backend calls Auth Backend: PUT /api/account/users/{email}/roles
   ↓
3. Auth Backend updates Keycloak user:
   - Assigns client roles (e.g., "approver", "faculty")
   - Sets approval_scopes attribute (e.g., ["research", "teaching"])
   ↓
4. Keycloak protocol mapper includes approval_scopes in JWT
   ↓
5. Faculty member gets JWT with:
   {
     "resource_access": { "ecs": { "roles": ["faculty", "approver"] } },
     "approval_scopes": ["research", "teaching"]
   }
   ↓
6. ECS Backend enforces scopes on approve/reject operations
   ↓
7. WorkPlan Approvals page shows only pending items matching scopes
```

- ECS backend enforces scope-based authorization
- ECS frontend provides admin and approver UIs

## Deployment Analysis

### Current Setup
**Woodpecker CI** (`auth-release.yml`) automatically deploys when a release tag is created:
- ✅ Builds Docker image with Jib
- ✅ Pushes to GHCR as `:1.0.19` and `:latest`
- ✅ Runs deployment step with individual `docker run` commands
- ❓ Deployment may have completed but containers aren't healthy

### Better Solution: Docker Compose Deployment

Yes! There's a `docker-compose.yml` in the auth repo. I can update Woodpecker CI to use it for cleaner deployment.

**Benefits of docker-compose:**
- Single command deployment: `docker-compose up -d`
- Easier to manage multiple services
- Configuration in version control
- Simpler rollback

### Let me update the deployment to use docker-compose:

## Solution: Watchtower or GitHub Actions with docker-compose

There are several options:

### Option 1: **Watchtower** (Simple, automatic)
A service that automatically pulls and deploys new images:
```bash
docker run -d --name watchtower \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  containrrr/watchtower \
  --interval 300 \
  --cleanup
```

name: github-release\n    image: alpine\n    environment:\n      GITHUB_TOKEN:\n        from_secret: github_token\n    commands:\n      - apk add --no-cache github-cli git\n      - |\n        VERSION=${CI_COMMIT_TAG}\n        PREV_TAG=$(git tag -l 'v*' --sort=-v:refname | grep -v 'spi-v' | grep -v 'release-v' | grep -v $VERSION | head -n1)\n        if [ -z \"$PREV_TAG\" ]; then\n          PREV_TAG=$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)\n        fi\n\n        echo \"# Changelog for $VERSION\" > release-assets/CHANGELOG.md\n        echo \"\" >> release-assets/CHANGELOG.md\n        git log $PREV_TAG..HEAD --pretty=format:\"- %s (%h)\" -- src/ build.gradle.kts >> release-assets/CHANGELOG.md || echo \"- No changes\" >> release-assets/CHANGELOG.md\n\n        if gh release view $CI_COMMIT_TAG --repo $CI_REPO > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n          gh release edit $CI_COMMIT_TAG --repo $CI_REPO --notes-file release-assets/CHANGELOG.md\n          gh release upload $CI_COMMIT_TAG --repo $CI_REPO --clobber release-assets/*\n        else\n          gh release create $CI_COMMIT_TAG \\\n            --repo $CI_REPO \\\n            --title \"Auth Backend $CI_COMMIT_TAG\" \\\n            --notes-file release-assets/CHANGELOG.md \\\n            release-assets/*\n        fi\n\n  - Based on the search results, here's what I found about Watchtower:

## Status

The Watchtower project has been officially archived and is no longer under active maintenance. The GitHub repository was switched to read-only status on December 17, 2025, marking the end of development for this widely used Docker container auto-update tool.

## Why It Was Archived

The developers announced they are archiving containrrr/watchtower because neither are big users of Docker anymore, and frankly lost interest (and time) in maintaining the project.

## Current Status

No future releases, bug fixes, or security updates are planned for Watchtower. However, existing Watchtower installations will continue to function.

## Alternatives and Successors

The search results mention several alternatives that users are migrating to:

1. What's Up Docker – a neat automation tool for detecting and updating new images in container collections
2. Diun (Docker Image Update Notifier), which tells when a new container image update is available but doesn't pull the new image, halt running containers, or restart anything

Additionally, there are a few forks out there, though some of the active forks have been noted as containing AI slop.

**About Watchtower:**
Yes, [Watchtower was archived on December 17, 2025](https://github.com/containrrr/watchtower/discussions/2135). The maintainers [lost interest and time](https://linuxiac.com/docker-update-tool-watchtower-reaches-end-of-maintenance/) as they stopped using Docker heavily.

- [**Diun**](https://www.xda-developers.com/watchtower-docker-updater-replacement-diun/) - Docker Image Update Notifier (notification-only)

services:
  auth-backend:
    image: ghcr.io/dsjkeeplearning/kos-auth-backend:latest
    container_name: auth-backend
    ports:
      - "8091:8080"
    environment:
      # Production database (update these with your actual values)
      - DB_HOST=${DB_HOST}
      - DB_PORT=${DB_PORT:-5432}
      - DB_NAME=${DB_NAME:-kos-auth}
      - DB_USERNAME=${DB_USERNAME}
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      # Production Keycloak
      - KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=${KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com}
      - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX=${KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/}
      - KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI=${KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/saas-admin}
      - SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=${SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET}
      # Disable OTEL for now
      - OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
    restart: unless-stopped

  auth-frontend:
    image: ghcr.io/dsjkeeplearning/kos-auth-backend-frontend:1.0.16
    container_name: auth-frontend
    ports:
      - "8090:80"
    restart: unless-stopped
```

> AGENT

The issue is clear: **The Woodpecker pipeline needs proper secrets configured, OR we need to manually create the `.env` file with real credentials.**

Current situation:
- ✅ docker-compose.yml exists in `/home/ubuntu/`  
- ❌ `.env` file missing (only `.env.production` template with placeholders)
- ❌ Auth backend crash-looping with `DB_PASSWORD=empty`

**Two options to fix this:**

### Option 1: Configure Woodpecker Secrets (Recommended for automation)
You need to add these secrets in your Woodpecker CI settings for the auth repo:
- `db_host` - Your PostgreSQL host
- `db_port` - PostgreSQL port  
- `db_name` - Database name
- `db_username` - DB username  
- `db_password` - **Actual DB password** (currently shows as "empty")
- `spring_profiles_active` - Should be `prod` not `dev`
- `keycloak_admin_client_secret` - Real client secret
- `saas_admin_client_secret` - Real client secret

Then retrigger the pipeline or create a new release tag.

### Option 2: Manual Fix (Immediate)
SSH into the server and create `.env` with real credentials:

```bash
ssh insight-service.jobin.wtf "cat > .env <<'EOF'
DB_HOST=<actual-db-host>
DB_PORT=5433
DB_NAME=kos-auth
DB_USERNAME=<actual-username>
DB_PASSWORD=<actual-password>
KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.keeplearningos.com
KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX=https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/
KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI=https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/master
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID=kos-admin-api
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=<actual-secret>
SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=<actual-secret>
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
EOF
docker-compose restart auth-backend"
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/dsj/auth/.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml",
  "content": "name: Deploy to Production\n\non:\n  release:\n    types: [published]\n\njobs:\n  deploy:\n    name: Deploy Auth Backend\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')\n\n    steps:\n      - name: Deploy to production server\n        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3\n        with:\n          host: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_HOST }}\n          username: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_USER }}\n          key: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_SSH_KEY }}\n          script: |\n            cd /home/ubuntu\n\n            # Create .env file from secrets\n            cat > .env <<'EOF'\n            DB_HOST=${{ secrets.DB_HOST }}\n            DB_PORT=${{ secrets.DB_PORT }}\n            DB_NAME=${{ secrets.DB_NAME }}\n            DB_USERNAME=${{ secrets.DB_USERNAME }}\n            DB_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}\n            KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL }}\n            KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX=${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX }}\n            KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI=${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI }}\n            KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID=${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID }}\n            KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET }}\n            SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=${{ secrets.SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET }}\n            SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=${{ secrets.SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE }}\n            OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true\n            EOF\n\n            # Login to GitHub Container Registry\n            echo \"${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\" | docker login ghcr.io -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin\n\n            # Pull latest images\n            docker-compose pull auth-backend\n\n            # Restart with new image\n            docker-compose up -d auth-backend\n\n            # Clean up old images\n            docker image prune -f\n\n            # Show status\n            docker-compose ps\n            docker logs auth-backend --tail 30\n"
}

  "content": "# Deployment Guide\n\n## Overview\n\n**CI:** Woodpecker (build, test, Docker image push, GitHub releases)\n**CD:** GitHub Actions (production deployment via SSH + docker-compose)\n\n## How It Works\n\n### 1. Create a Release\n```bash\ngit tag -a v1.0.X -m \"Release v1.0.X: Description\"\ngit push origin v1.0.X\n```\n\n### 2. Automated Pipeline\n1. **Woodpecker CI** (on tag push):\n   - Builds JAR with Gradle\n   - Pushes Docker image to GHCR (versioned + latest tags)\n   - Creates GitHub release with changelog\n   - Uploads JAR artifacts\n\n2. **GitHub Actions** (on release published):\n   - SSHs into production server\n   - Creates `.env` file from GitHub secrets\n   - Pulls latest Docker image\n   - Restarts auth-backend via docker-compose\n   - Shows deployment status\n\n## Required GitHub Secrets\n\nConfigure these in: `Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Repository secrets`\n\n### SSH Access\n| Secret | Example Value | Description |\n|--------|---------------|-------------|\n| `PRODUCTION_HOST` | `insight-service.jobin.wtf` | Production server hostname/IP |\n| `PRODUCTION_USER` | `ubuntu` | SSH username |\n| `PRODUCTION_SSH_KEY` | `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----...` | SSH private key (full PEM format) |\n\n### Database\n| Secret | Example Value | Description |\n|--------|---------------|-------------|\n| `DB_HOST` | `172.17.0.1` | PostgreSQL host (Docker bridge or external) |\n| `DB_PORT` | `5433` | PostgreSQL port |\n| `DB_NAME` | `kos-auth` | Database name |\n| `DB_USERNAME` | `postgres` | Database username |\n| `DB_PASSWORD` | `your-secure-password` | Database password |\n\n### Keycloak\n| Secret | Example Value | Description |\n|--------|---------------|-------------|\n| `KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL` | `https://auth.keeplearningos.com` | Keycloak base URL |\n| `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX` | `https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/` | JWT issuer prefix |\n| `KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI` | `https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/master` | SaaS admin realm issuer |\n| `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID` | `kos-admin-api` | Admin client ID |\n| `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` | `your-client-secret` | Admin client secret |\n| `SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` | `your-saas-secret` | SaaS admin client secret |\n\n### Spring Profile\n| Secret | Example Value | Description |\n|--------|---------------|-------------|\n| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | `prod` | Spring profile (use `prod` for production) |\n\n## Manual Deployment (Emergency)\n\nIf GitHub Actions fails, deploy manually:\n\n```bash\nssh insight-service.jobin.wtf\ncd /home/ubuntu\n\n# Create .env with production values\ncat > .env <<'EOF'\nDB_HOST=172.17.0.1\nDB_PORT=5433\nDB_NAME=kos-auth\nDB_USERNAME=postgres\nDB_PASSWORD=your-password\nKEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.keeplearningos.com\nKEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX=https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/\nKEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI=https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/master\nKEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID=kos-admin-api\nKEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=your-secret\nSAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=your-secret\nSPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod\nOTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true\nEOF\n\n# Pull and restart\ndocker-compose pull auth-backend\ndocker-compose up -d auth-backend\ndocker logs auth-backend --tail 50\n```\n\n## Monitoring\n\nCheck deployment status:\n```bash\nssh insight-service.jobin.wtf \"docker ps | grep auth-backend\"\nssh insight-service.jobin.wtf \"docker logs auth-backend --tail 100\"\n```\n\nHealth check:\n```bash\ncurl https://api.forge.keeplearningos.com/actuator/health\n```\n\n## Rollback\n\nTo rollback to a previous version:\n\n```bash\nssh insight-service.jobin.wtf\ncd /home/ubuntu\n\n# Edit docker-compose.yml to use specific version tag\n# Change: image: ghcr.io/dsjkeeplearning/kos-auth-backend:latest\n# To:     image: ghcr.io/dsjkeeplearning/kos-auth-backend:1.0.19\n\ndocker-compose pull auth-backend\ndocker-compose up -d auth-backend\n```\n\nOr retag and redeploy:\n```bash\ngit tag -d v1.0.X                    # Delete local tag\ngit push origin :refs/tags/v1.0.X    # Delete remote tag\ngit tag -a v1.0.X <commit-hash> -m \"Rollback\"\ngit push origin v1.0.X              # Trigger new deployment\n```\n"
}

## ✅ What I Did

### 1. Created GitHub Actions Deployment Workflow
**File:** `.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml`

### 2. Updated Woodpecker CI
**File:** `.woodpecker/auth-release.yml`
- **Removed** deployment step
- **Kept** build, Docker push, and GitHub release creation
- Added comment: "Deployment handled by GitHub Actions"

### 3. Created Deployment Documentation
**File:** `.github/DEPLOYMENT.md`
- Complete list of required GitHub secrets
- Manual deployment instructions
- Monitoring and rollback procedures

## 🔧 Next Steps: Configure GitHub Secrets

You need to add these secrets in your GitHub repo:
**Go to:** `Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Repository secrets`

### Required Secrets:
```
SSH Access:
  - PRODUCTION_HOST (e.g., insight-service.jobin.wtf)
  - PRODUCTION_USER (e.g., ubuntu)
  - PRODUCTION_SSH_KEY (your SSH private key in PEM format)

Database:
  - DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD

Keycloak:
  - KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL
  - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX
  - KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI
  - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID
  - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET
  - SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET

Spring:
  - SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE (set to "prod")
```

> AGENT

Good question! Let me explain the current flow and then we can adjust if needed.

**Current flow (in `auth-release.yml`):**
1. On tag push → Woodpecker builds JAR + pushes Docker image
2. Woodpecker creates GitHub release with changelog using `gh CLI`
3. GitHub release published → triggers GitHub Actions deployment

**Why Woodpecker creates the release:**
- It already has the built JARs to upload as artifacts
- Can generate changelog from git commits
- Single pipeline handles build → image → release

**Alternative approach:**
We could let GitHub Actions handle everything instead:
- Tag push → GitHub Actions builds, pushes image, creates release, deploys
- Woodpecker only for PR builds/tests

Which do you prefer:
1. **Keep current**: Woodpecker = build+release, GitHub Actions = deploy only
2. **GitHub Actions only**: Remove Woodpecker release pipeline entirely
3. **Simplify Woodpecker**: Just build+push Docker, let GitHub create release + deploy

## How GitHub Actions Deploys to EC2:

1. **Trigger**: GitHub release published
2. **SSH Action**: Uses `appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3` to connect
3. **Remote Commands**: 
   - Creates `.env` file with secrets
   - Pulls Docker image from GHCR
   - Runs `docker-compose up -d`
   - Shows logs

Aha! Your server uses **Cloudflare Tunnel** for SSH access. GitHub Actions can't use `cloudflared` proxy.

**Two options:**

### Option 1: Use Direct EC2 IP (if accessible)
Do you have a direct public IP or VPN access to the EC2 instance?

### Option 2: Self-hosted GitHub Actions Runner (Better for Cloudflare Tunnel)
Run a GitHub Actions runner ON the EC2 instance itself. Then deployment is local:

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: self-hosted  # Runs on your EC2
    steps:
      - name: Deploy locally
        run: |
          cd /home/ubuntu
          cat > .env <<EOF
          # ... secrets from ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}
          EOF
          docker-compose pull && docker-compose up -d
```

**Which approach do you prefer?**  
Or I can set up a webhook-based deployment (simple HTTP endpoint on EC2 that GitHub calls)?

> DEVELOPER

what do you think of this? is it helpful?

> AGENT

Honestly? **We made a strategic mistake.** Let me explain why:

## The Irony

**Woodpecker is ALREADY running on your EC2 instance** (we saw `woodpecker-server` running there). So:

- ✅ **Woodpecker on EC2** = Local docker access, perfect for deployment
- ❌ **GitHub Actions** = Remote, can't SSH through Cloudflare Tunnel

We essentially moved deployment FROM a tool that has direct local access TO a tool that needs complex network setup. That's backwards!

## Better Approaches (ranked):

### 1. **Revert: Woodpecker for Deploy, GitHub Actions for CI** ⭐ Recommended
- **Woodpecker** (on EC2): Handles deployment via local docker commands
- **GitHub Actions**: Build, test, create releases (no deployment)
- Simple, works with your existing Cloudflare Tunnel setup
- No new infrastructure needed

### 2. **Self-hosted GitHub Actions Runner**
- Install runner on EC2, deployment becomes local
- Pros: GitHub-native, good audit trail
- Cons: Runner maintenance, security considerations, resource usage
- Essentially reinventing what Woodpecker already does

### 3. **Webhook Deployment**
- EC2 listens for GitHub webhook → pulls + restarts
- Pros: Simple, lightweight
- Cons: Less features than Woodpecker, manual security setup

## My Recommendation

**Go back to Woodpecker for deployment.** It's already there, has docker socket access, works perfectly. Use GitHub Actions only for building and creating releases.

The original separation idea was good—but we separated in the wrong direction!

**Want me to revert the deployment back to Woodpecker?**

> DEVELOPER

what do you think about https://crazymax.dev/diun/ for remote docker update? will it benefit us?

> AGENT

Good question! Let me analyze if Diun fits your use case:

## What Diun Does

**Diun = Notification-only** (successor to Watchtower, which was archived)
- Monitors registries for new image versions
- Sends notifications (Discord, Slack, email, webhook)
- **Does NOT** pull or restart containers automatically

## Your Current Need

You want: **Automated deployment on release** → Pull image → Restart containers

## Would Diun Help?

**Short answer: No, it solves a different problem.**

### Why Diun Doesn't Fit:

1. **Notification ≠ Automation**
   - Diun tells you "new image available"
   - You still need something to DO the deployment
   - Adds complexity without solving the core issue

2. **Wrong Trigger**
   - Your trigger: "I created a release" → deploy
   - Diun's trigger: "Registry has new image" → notify
   - You control both sides, so notifications are redundant

3. **Cloudflare Tunnel Problem Remains**
   - Diun runs on EC2 and notifies you
   - Still need remote access to deploy
   - Doesn't solve the GitHub Actions SSH issue

### Diun Use Cases (not your scenario):

✅ Monitoring **third-party** images (postgres, redis, nginx)  
✅ Manual approval before deployment  
✅ Staged rollouts with human oversight  
✅ Multi-environment deployments (dev → staging → prod)

## Better Options for You:

### Option 1: **Woodpecker Deployment** (Simplest) ⭐
```
Tag v1.0.x → Woodpecker builds → Woodpecker deploys locally
```
- Already on EC2, direct docker access
- No network issues, no new services

### Option 2: **GitHub Actions + Webhook**
```
Tag → GH Actions builds → Calls webhook → EC2 script deploys
```
- Simple HTTP endpoint on EC2
- Works through Cloudflare Tunnel
- Lightweight alternative to Diun

### Option 3: **Diun + Automation** (Overengineered)
```
Tag → Build → Image pushed → Diun detects → Webhook → Deploy
```
- Extra hop (Diun) adds latency and complexity
- More moving parts to maintain

## My Recommendation

**Don't use Diun for this.** You need **automation**, not **notification**.

Diun is great for monitoring external dependencies, but you're deploying your own service where you control the release process.

**Stick with Woodpecker for deployment** or build a simple webhook if you want GitHub Actions integration.

**Question:** Do you want me to set up a lightweight webhook deployment endpoint instead? It's simpler than Diun and solves your actual problem.

services:
  auth-backend:
    image: ghcr.io/dsjkeeplearning/kos-auth-backend:latest
    container_name: auth-backend
    ports:
      - "8091:8080"
    environment:
      # Production database (update these with your actual values)
      - DB_HOST=${DB_HOST}
      - DB_PORT=${DB_PORT:-5432}
      - DB_NAME=${DB_NAME:-kos-auth}
      - DB_USERNAME=${DB_USERNAME}
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      # Production Keycloak
      - KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=${KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com}
      - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX=${KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_PREFIX:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/}
      - KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI=${KEYCLOAK_SAAS_ISSUER_URI:-https://auth.keeplearningos.com/realms/saas-admin}
      - SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=${SAAS_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET}
      # Disable OTEL for now
      - OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true

- ⚠️ Auth backend had a Keycloak connection error at startup (401 Unauthorized)
- ⚠️ The `/api/super/**` endpoints require **ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN** authentication

## Quick Diagnostic Steps

**Option 1: Check browser console (fastest)**
1. Open auth frontend in browser
2. Press F12 → Network tab
3. Navigate to Users page
4. Look for the `/api/super/realms/kos/users` request
5. Check the response:
   - **401/403** = Not authenticated/authorized
   - **200 with empty array** = Auth working but no users returned
   - **500** = Server error

**Option 2: Test API directly**
```bash
# From your machine (if you have a valid token)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  https://api.forge.keeplearningos.com/api/super/realms/kos/users
```

**Option 3: Restart auth backend** (to fix Keycloak connection)
```bash
ssh insight-service.jobin.wtf "cd /home/ubuntu && docker compose restart auth-backend"
```

> AGENT

Perfect! ✅ Keycloak connectivity is now working! The logs show:
- "Keycloak is available, starting sync..."
- "Full sync completed: 1 realms processed, success=true"
- "Startup sync completed successfully: 1 realms synced"

No more 401 errors! The auth backend successfully connected to Keycloak on the internal network.

The issue was that the docker-compose.yml was missing `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID` and `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variables, so the auth backend couldn't authenticate with Keycloak's admin API.

**Fixed:**
1. ✅ Updated KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL to internal URL (`http://172.17.0.1:8088`)
2. ✅ Added missing environment variables to docker-compose.yml
3. ✅ Recreated container to apply changes
4. ✅ Keycloak sync running successfully

Now users should be visible in the auth frontend at **https://insight-service.jobin.wtf:8090**. Navigate to "Realms" → "kos" → "Users" to see the 8 users that exist in the database.

    17→@Service

    24→    private val logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(UserService::class.java)
    25→
    26→    suspend fun listUsers(realmName: String): List<RealmUserResponse> {
    27→        val realm = realmRepository.findByRealmName(realmName).awaitSingleOrNull()
    28→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Realm '$realmName' not found")
    29→
    30→        val users = userRepository.findByRealmId(realm.id!!)
    31→            .collectList().awaitSingle()
    32→
    33→        return users.map { user ->
    34→            val authorizedClients = getAuthorizedClientsForUser(user.id!!)
    35→            user.toResponse(authorizedClients)
    36→        }
    37→    }
    38→
    39→    suspend fun getUser(realmName: String, userId: UUID): RealmUserDetailResponse {
    40→        val realm = realmRepository.findByRealmName(realmName).awaitSingleOrNull()
    41→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Realm '$realmName' not found")
    42→
    43→        val user = userRepository.findById(userId).awaitSingleOrNull()
    44→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "User not found")
    45→
    46→        if (user.realmId != realm.id) {
    47→            throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "User not found in realm")
    48→        }
    49→
    50→        val authorizedClients = getAuthorizedClientDetailsForUser(user.id!!)
    51→        return user.toDetailResponse(authorizedClients)
    52→    }
    53→
    54→    suspend fun getUserByEmail(realmName: String, email: String): RealmUserDetailResponse {
    55→        val realm = realmRepository.findByRealmName(realmName).awaitSingleOrNull()
    56→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Realm '$realmName' not found")
    57→
    58→        val user = userRepository.findByRealmIdAndEmail(realm.id!!, email).awaitSingleOrNull()
    59→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "User not found")
    60→
    61→        val authorizedClients = getAuthorizedClientDetailsForUser(user.id!!)
    62→        return user.toDetailResponse(authorizedClients)
    63→    }
    64→
    65→    suspend fun createUser(
    66→        realmName: String,
    67→        request: CreateRealmUserRequest,
    68→        actorKeycloakId: String
    69→    ): RealmUserDetailResponse {
    70→        val realm = realmRepository.findByRealmName(realmName).awaitSingleOrNull()
    71→            ?: throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Realm '$realmName' not found")
    72→
    73→        // Check if user already exists
    74→        val existingUser = userRepository.findByRealmIdAndEmail(realm.id!!, request.email).awaitSingleOrNull()
    75→        if (existingUser != null) {
    76→            throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "User with email '${request.email}' already exists")
    77→        }
    78→
    79→        // Create user (keycloakUserId will be empty until they actually log in)
    80→        val user = userRepository.save(
    81→            User(
    82→                keycloakUserId = "", // Will be populated when user logs in via Keycloak
    83→                email = request.email,
    84→                displayName = request.displayName,
    85→                firstName = request.firstName,
    86→                lastName = request.lastName,
    87→                phone = request.phone,
    88→                jobTitle = request.jobTitle,
    89→                department = request.department,
    90→                accountId = realm.accountId ?: realm.id, // Use realm id if no account
    91→                realmId = realm.id,
    92→                status = "ACTIVE"
    93→            )
    94→        ).awaitSingle()
    95→
    96→        logger.info("Created user ${request.email} in realm $realmName")
    97→
    98→        // Assign to clients if specified
    99→        for (clientId in request.clientIds) {
   100→            val client = clientRepository.findById(clientId).awaitSingleOrNull()
   101→            if (client != null && client.realmId == realm.id) {
   102→                userClientRepository.save(
   103→                    KcUserClient(
   104→                        realmId = realm.id,
   105→                        userKeycloakId = "",
   106→                        userEmail = request.email,
   107→                        clientId = clientId,
   108→                        assignedByKeycloakId = actorKeycloakId
   109→                    )
   110→                ).awaitSingle()
   111→                logger.info("Assigned user ${request.email} to client ${client.clientId}")
   112→            }
   113→        }
   114→
   115→        val authorizedClients = getAuthorizedClientDetailsForUser(user.id!!)
   116→        return user.toDetailResponse(authorizedClients)
   117→    }

**FOUND IT!** The issue is that the `UserService.listUsers()` method (line 26-36) queries users from the **auth backend's local database**, NOT from Keycloak directly!

```kotlin
val users = userRepository.findByRealmId(realm.id!!)
    .collectList().awaitSingle()
```

The local `users` table is populated by:
1. Users created via the auth backend API
2. Users synced from Keycloak (if the sync process includes users)

> AGENT

The patched auth backend is now running and successfully connected to Keycloak. The fix changes the `UserService.listUsers()` method to fetch users directly from Keycloak's Admin API instead of querying the empty local database.

**What was the problem:**
- The auth backend was querying its local `users` table which was empty
- The Keycloak sync process only syncs realms, clients, roles, and groups - NOT users
- Users exist in Keycloak but weren't being synced to the auth backend

**The fix:**
- Modified `UserService.listUsers()` to call `keycloakAdminClient.getUsers(realmName)` 
- This fetches users directly from Keycloak instead of the local database
- Returns up to 1000 users per realm

Please test by accessing **https://forge.keeplearningos.com/realms** and navigating to either the "kos" or "master" realm - you should now see the user lists!

> AGENT

Perfect! ✅ The updated backend is running with the complete fix. I've updated three methods:

1. **`listUsers()`** - Fetches users from Keycloak and uses the Keycloak user ID as the UUID
2. **`getUser()`** - Fetches individual user details directly from Keycloak (fixes the crash)
3. **`getUserByEmail()`** - Also fetches from Keycloak instead of the empty local database

Now try again:
- Navigate to **https://forge.keeplearningos.com/realms/kos/users**
- You should see the user list
- Click on any user - the detail page should now load without crashing

The backend is now fully fetching all user data from Keycloak instead of the empty local database!
